_meta.indication: MOVANTIK (naloxegol) is indicated for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation (OIC) in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study of two doses (12.5 mg and 25 mg) of naloxegol for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with opioid-induced constipation (OIC) and non-cancer related pain receiving an opioid morphine equivalent daily dose of 30 to 1,000 mg for at least four weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Response defined as >=3 SBMs per week and a change from baseline of >=1 SBM per week for at least 9 out of the 12 study weeks and 3 out of the last 4 weeks
pivotal_trials.n: N=652 randomized 1:1:1 (placebo 214, naloxegol 12.5 mg 213, naloxegol 25 mg 214 in the ITT set)
pivotal_trials.result: Responders: placebo 63 (29%), 12.5 mg 87 (41%; difference 11.4%, 95% CI 2.4%, 20.4%; p=0.015), 25 mg 95 (44%; difference 15.0%, 95% CI 5.9%, 24.0%; p=0.001) [labeled Study 1]

nct_ctgov.title: Assessment of Efficacy and Safety in Patients With Non-cancer-related Pain and Opioid-induced Constipation

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study of 12.5 mg and 25 mg naloxegol once daily for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with OIC and non-cancer related pain
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Response defined as >=3 SBMs per week and a change from baseline of >=1 SBM per week for at least 9 out of the 12 study weeks and 3 out of the last 4 weeks
pivotal_trials.n: 700 patients randomized; labeled Study 2 each arm N=232 (placebo, 12.5 mg, 25 mg)
pivotal_trials.result: Responders: placebo 68 (29%), 12.5 mg 81 (35%; difference 5.6%, 95% CI -2.9%, 14.1%; p=0.202, not significant), 25 mg 92 (40%; difference 10.3%, 95% CI 1.7%, 18.9%; p=0.021)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=3%): abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, flatulence, vomiting, and headache. In pooled Studies 1 and 2, abdominal pain occurred in 21% (25 mg) and 12% (12.5 mg) vs 7% placebo; diarrhea 9% vs 5%. Possible opioid withdrawal occurred in 3% (14/446) of the 25 mg group vs <1% placebo.
target_moa: Naloxegol is a PEGylated derivative of naloxone that acts as an antagonist of opioid binding at the mu-opioid receptor, functioning as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (PAMORA) in the gastrointestinal tract to decrease the constipating effects of opioids.

advisory_committee.vote: The Anesthesia and Analgesia Drug Products Advisory Committee (AADAC) met June 11-12, 2014 to discuss the cardiovascular safety of five peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonists in development for OIC in chronic non-cancer pain, including Movantik; the meeting was a class-wide discussion and no product-specific efficacy vote is recorded.

summary.text: Naloxegol (Movantik), a new molecular entity, was approved September 2014 under a standard review NDA 204760 (received September 16, 2013) for OIC in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain, based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (Studies 04 and 05); approval included a required post-marketing MACE safety study.

citations.quote: Movantik (naloxegol), an opioid antagonist, contains naloxegol oxalate as the active ingredient. (Naloxegol is a PEGylated derivative of naloxol.) Naloxegol is considered a new molecular entity (NME).

The evaluation of efficacy was based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled controlled trials (Study 004 and Study 005) in patients with opioid-induced-constipation (OIC) and non-cancer related pain.

requirement.text: 2779-1: A post-marketing, observational epidemiologic study comparing MOVANTIK to other OIC treatments in chronic non-cancer pain patients, with a primary outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: CV death, nonfatal MI, and nonfatal stroke).

citations.quote: 2779-1 A post-marketing, observational epidemiologic study comparing MOVANTIK (naloxegol) to other treatments of opioid induced constipation in patients with chronic non-cancer pain. The study's primary outcome is a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): cardiovascular (CV) death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke.

requirement.text: 2779-2: An in vitro study to evaluate the time-dependent/mechanism-based inhibition potential of naloxegol on the hepatic CYP2C8 enzyme.
